docs.title: 0. Executive summary
docs.text:
68 findings: 7 Critical, 16 High, 26 Medium/Low, 19 correctness bugs.

# Theme What is actually happening 1 Fake / simulation-grade crypto presented as real Kyber KEM returns unrelated random secrets; AEAD fallbacks return zero-filled ciphertext with a random tag; Poly1305 is truncated SHA-256; C container "signature verify" ignores the public key and accepts zero-length signatures; "AES-GCM" transport is a repeating-key XOR with no MAC. 2 Fail-open authentication and update installation Inference FastAPI app never runs its own lifespan (so security is None and require_auth allows everyone); Model Hub boots with admin/admin, binds 0.0.0.0, and prints the admin key; Python install_update() never checks the verified flag. 3 Memory-safety bugs inside the security layer itself C SBOM JSON export underflows out_len - pos and writes out of bounds; SBOM hashing reads past a 256-byte stack buffer; manifest parser uses strncmp on a length-bounded buffer; secure allocator loses tracking records permanently and has unchecked size arithmetic. 4 Silent numerical corruption in training Scheduler LRs never reach param_groups; distributed collectives are no-ops; FSDP nulls live gradients; checkpoint_sequential runs layers in the wrong order; DataLoader(num_workers>0) ignores batch_size; several optimizers have wrong update math. 5 Assurance documentation contradicts reality docs/ARCHITECTURE.md marks all ten S0–S9 layers Status: Complete while SECURITY.md calls them experimental/partial/not verified/not audited. PQC code is labelled FIPS 203/204/205 despite the repo's own note that it is not interoperable.

Highest-priority single fixes: C-1 (C container verify), C-2 (Python unsigned update install), C-3 (hub default admin), C-4/C-5 (fake KEM/AEAD), C-6 (inference auth fail-open), C-7 (XOR "AES-GCM").

docs.title: C-1 — Container image signature verification ignores the public key and accepts an empty signature
docs.text:
Severity: Critical · Status: [R] · Location: security/updates/container_security.c:77-84 (declared include/neural_core/security/container_security.h:88)

int SNEPPX_container_verify_image(const uint8_t *manifest, size_t manifest_len,
    const uint8_t *signature, size_t sig_len, const uint8_t *pubkey) {
    if (!manifest || !signature || !pubkey) return -1;
    uint8_t hash[32];
    SNEPPX_sha256(hash, manifest, manifest_len);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < 32 && i < sig_len; i++)
        if (signature[i] != hash[i]) return 1;
    return 0;
}

Why broken: pubkey is never used. The "signature" is compared directly to the manifest's SHA-256 digest, so no private key is involved. Worse, the loop bound i < sig_len means sig_len == 0 executes zero comparisons and returns 0 (success). sig_len between 1 and 31 accepts a matching prefix. The header documents 0 on success, -1 on error, but the implementation returns 1 for mismatch, so the error convention is inconsistent too.

Scenario: Replace an image manifest, set signature = SHA256(manifest) (or pass sig_len = 0) with any non-NULL pubkey → verification returns success and a malicious image is trusted.

Suggested fix: Require sig_len == SNEPPX_ED25519_SIGNATURE_LEN, hash with domain separation, call SNEPPX_ed25519_verify(pubkey, digest, 32, sig), and use a single documented convention (0 valid, -1 invalid arg, 1 invalid signature). Add tests for empty/truncated/wrong-key signatures.

docs.title: C-2 — Python update manager stages and installs unsigned images; verified flag is never enforced
docs.text:
Severity: Critical · Status: [R] · Location: bindings/python/SneppX_ALG/interface_bindings/container_security.py:713-747, 749-797

# stage_update()
if signature_path and not self.verify_signature(str(dest), signature_path):
    ...
"verified": signature_path is not None,
...
# install_update() — meta["verified"] is never read
subprocess.run(["dd", f"if={update_file}", f"of={part_path}", "bs=4M", ...], check=True)

Why broken: signature_path defaults to None; when omitted, verification is skipped and staging reports success. meta["verified"] = False is written but no code path reads it. install_update() writes whatever bytes are staged to the inactive rootfs partition with dd and switches the boot slot. A caller (or an attacker able to replace staged content) gets unsigned code execution on next boot. The class is presented as "Signed update management with rollback support".

Related: update_id is interpolated into update_dir / "staged" / update_id and later into a shutil.move destination without validation (:721, :754, :793) → directory-level path traversal (see M-5).

Suggested fix: Fail staging when no signature/trusted key is configured; re-verify the staged bytes immediately before dd; reject meta.get("verified") is not True; validate update_id against ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$.

docs.title: C-3 — Model Hub: admin/admin by default, public bind, raw admin key printed to stdout
docs.text:
Severity: Critical · Status: [R] (hub API) / [A] (CLI bind) · Location: model_hub/api/main.py:263-288, :351-358; model_hub/cli/main.py:575-576, :605-607

admin_user = os.environ.get("SNEPPX_HUB_ADMIN_USER", "admin")
admin_pass = os.environ.get("SNEPPX_HUB_ADMIN_PASSWORD", "admin")
...
fresh_key = db.bootstrap_admin()
if fresh_key:
    print(f"[sneppx-hub] Created default admin user + API key: {fresh_key}")

p_srv.add_argument("--host", default="0.0.0.0")
uvicorn.run(app, host=args.host, port=args.port, workers=args.workers)

Why broken: Startup automatically creates an admin account with a publicly known password and logs a fully privileged API key in cleartext. Combined with the 0.0.0.0 default, anyone who can reach the port can authenticate; anyone with log access gets the key. With multiple workers, the JSON store has no cross-process lock, so bootstrap can race.

Suggested fix: Refuse to start if SNEPPX_HUB_ADMIN_PASSWORD is unset (or generate a CSPRNG password written to a 0600 file); default --host to 127.0.0.1; never print raw keys (print a fingerprint only).

docs.title: C-4 — Kyber KEM and X25519 fallback fabricate keys and shared secrets
docs.text:
Severity: Critical · Status: [R] · Location: bindings/python/SneppX_ALG/interface_bindings/crypto_kem.py:38-52, :60-90

def encapsulate(self, pk):
    ct = os.urandom(ct_size); ss = os.urandom(32); return ct, ss
def decapsulate(self, sk, ct):
    return os.urandom(32)
...
except ImportError:
    sk = os.urandom(32) if private is None else private
    pk = os.urandom(32)          # unrelated to sk
...
except ImportError:
    return os.urandom(32)        # dh() ignores both inputs

Why broken: No C backend is called despite the "wraps the C implementations" docstring. Encapsulation and decapsulation produce independent random values, so two parties can never agree on a key. The X25519 fallback generates a public key unrelated to its private key. This is worse than an error: code that derives keys from one side's output silently gets no confidentiality. (crypto_sign.py demonstrates the correct fail-closed pattern — use it as the model.)

Suggested fix: Call the real binding, or raise RuntimeError when unavailable. Never synthesize keys/ciphertexts/secrets with os.urandom.

docs.title: C-5 — AES-GCM / ChaCha20-Poly1305 fallbacks emit unencrypted data and skip authentication
docs.text:
Severity: Critical · Status: [R] · Location: bindings/python/SneppX_ALG/interface_bindings/crypto_symmetric.py:33-51, :65-83

except ImportError:
    ct = bytes(len(plaintext))   # zeros — plaintext never encrypted
    tag = os.urandom(16)
    return iv + ct + tag
...
except ImportError:
    return ciphertext[12:-16]    # no tag verification at all

Why broken: The documented AEAD guarantee is confidentiality and integrity. The fallback writes zero bytes, appends a random tag, and decrypt() returns caller-supplied bytes unchanged with no MAC check. There is no error signal: a caller cannot tell it was not authenticated. cryptography is currently a hard dependency so this is latent in a normal install, but it is reachable in degraded/partial environments and is exported as a security primitive. Caller-supplied nonce (nonce or os.urandom(12)) also permits nonce reuse.

Suggested fix: Delete both fallbacks (or raise). Enforce unique nonces and verify tags in all paths.

docs.title: C-6 — Inference API authentication fails open: lifespan never registered
docs.text:
Severity: Critical · Status: [R] · Location: bindings/python/SneppX_ALG/interface_bindings/inference_server.py:315-323, :391-420

def require_auth(request):
    sec = get_security()
    if sec is None:
        return None          # <-- request allowed
...
@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):   # defines initialization of _security
    ...
app = FastAPI(title="SneppX Inference API", version="1.5.3")  # no lifespan=

Why broken: A grep for lifespan in the whole file returns only the function definition at line 392. The hook is never attached, so _security stays None for any process that imports app directly (e.g. uvicorn ...:app). require_auth then returns None without rejecting, and FirewallASGIMiddleware's body/header limits are bypassed by the same security_getter() is None path. serve_cli.py configures security in the parent process, but --reload / --workers > 1 reimport the module in children and lose it ([A]).

Suggested fix: Pass lifespan=lifespan to FastAPI(...); make require_auth raise 503 (not allow) when _security is None; initialize auth from environment at import as a fallback; use an app factory so workers inherit configuration.

docs.title: C-7 — "AES-GCM" transport mode is a repeating-key XOR stream with no MAC
docs.text:
Severity: Critical · Status: [R] · Location: security/network/transport_security.c:157-159, :201-203, :342-350

if (use_aes_gcm) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < len; i++)
        ciphertext[i] = plaintext[i] ^ s->session_key[i % SNEPPX_TLS_KEY_LEN];
}

Why broken: No AES, no nonce, no authentication tag. The keystream repeats every 32 bytes. Ciphertext is malleable (flip one byte → flip one plaintext bit with no integrity failure) and leaks plaintext relationships (C1 xor C2 == P1 xor P2). SNEPPX_transport_set_cipher_type(1) enables it. Default mode uses real ChaCha20, and the setter is not in the public header with no in-tree callers — so reachability is latent, but it is compiled and callable via an external declaration.

Suggested fix: Remove the XOR path; implement AES-GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305 with unique nonce, AAD, and tag verification; otherwise return -1 when the AEAD backend is unavailable.

docs.title: H-1 — SBOM JSON export: size_t underflow → out-of-bounds write [R]
docs.text: security/updates/container_security.c:212-227. snprintf returns the required length, not bytes written. After pos += snprintf(...), a long formatted string makes pos > out_len; the next call gets out_len - pos, which wraps to near SIZE_MAX, and writes the full JSON past the caller's buffer. pos < out_len in the loop does not protect the trailing " ]\n}\n" write. Call SNEPPX_sbom_export_json(doc, buf, 16) → heap/stack corruption. Fix: track remaining, bail with -1 when need >= remaining, advance pos only by bytes actually written.

docs.title: H-2 — SBOM component hash: OOB stack read and NULL dereference [R]
docs.text: security/updates/container_security.c:180-182. hlen = snprintf(hash_input, 256, "%s:%s:%s", name, version, type); if the formatted length exceeds 255, SNEPPX_sha256 reads past the 256-byte buffer. version/type are passed raw here although the copies above default them for NULL, so NULL inputs fault. Fix: reject hlen >= 256, or hash incrementally; use the defaulted pointers in the format call.

docs.title: H-3 — Model metadata controls client filesystem paths and honors file:// [R]
docs.text: model_hub/storage/backend.py:125-129, :166-173; model_hub/api/main.py:438-504; model_hub/api/models.py:127-135. _full_path() does normpath(key).lstrip("/") then join(base, clean) — no containment check, and download_file() explicitly allows key.startswith("file://") to set src to an arbitrary host path. A malicious model-card files[].url / files[].filename (no validation on ModelFile) makes a downloading victim copy e.g. /etc/passwd to an attacker-chosen ../../ destination. SHA checking limits overwrites to known-content files but does not stop disclosure. Fix: basename-only filenames, resolve-and-verify containment, reject file:// and non-storage keys, validate card entries server-side.

docs.title: H-4 — Rekey desynchronizes peers after 1000 messages [R]
docs.text: security/network/transport_security.c:167-175 vs :189-213. Encrypt increments session_rekey_counter and rotates the session key; decrypt never counts or rotates. On message 1001 the receiver still has the old key → all subsequent traffic is garbage, permanently. Fix: derive per-message keys from a sequence number tracked on both sides and authenticate the sequence.

docs.title: H-5 — encrypt_with_aad produces undecryptable output and can dereference NULL AAD [R]
docs.text: security/network/transport_security.c:366-396. The ChaCha20 nonce is XORed with AAD bytes, but the normal decrypt path reinitializes with the original nonce and there is no decrypt-with-AAD counterpart → garbage. aad is not checked before memcpy(session_aad_keys[...], aad, ...) → crash for aad == NULL. Fix: paired decrypt-with-AAD using the same derived nonce, real MAC over AAD, validate aad != NULL || aad_len == 0.

docs.title: H-6 — "Privacy defenses" use fixed-seed noise that is trivially removable [A]
docs.text: bindings/python/SneppX_ALG/interface_bindings/s5_safety.py:193-210, :569-602. np.random.RandomState(0) is recreated inside every call, so the same noise vector is applied every time; identical inputs give identical outputs. An adversary who reads the public code subtracts the exact noise and recovers original gradients/logits. Confirmed by agent probe with _HAS_C_S5 == False. Fix: OS-seeded np.random.default_rng() or caller-supplied CSPRNG; verify the C path does not repeat the design.

docs.title: H-7 — S5 native library loaded from environment/CWD at import [R]
docs.text: bindings/python/SneppX_ALG/interface_bindings/s5_safety.py:29-61. search_dirs includes os.environ["SNEPPX_SECURITY_LIB"] and ".", with bare-name ctypes.CDLL(name) fallback. Library initializers execute with process privileges at import time → env manipulation or CWD DLL planting = code execution. Fix: only accept an explicit admin-configured absolute path, validate containment, drop "." and bare-name fallback.

docs.title: H-8 — Argon2 silently downgrades to 300-iteration PBKDF2 (active here) [R]
docs.text: bindings/python/SneppX_ALG/interface_bindings/crypto_kdf.py:91-106; argon2 is not a dependency and is absent. Every Argon2.hash() call is actually PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with time_cost*100 = 300 iterations, ignoring mem_cost and parallelism. The same module's PBKDF2.derive defaults to 600,000 iterations. Offline attacks are trivial and callers get no indication. Fix: raise when the real backend is missing, or expose an explicitly-named pbkdf2_sha256_300 with a stored algorithm identifier and strong parameters.

docs.title: H-9 — Tamper-evident audit chains are forgeable [A]
docs.text: bindings/python/SneppX_ALG/interface_bindings/audit_logger.py:287-303, :883-905; key_vault.py:60-65. Hash chain uses unkeyed SHA-256 over fields stored next to the digest → anyone who can edit the log can recompute the chain. key_vault.AuditLogger.verify_chain() only compares prev_hash linkage and never recomputes hashes or re-reads the persisted file. audit_logger only checks query(limit=10000) so older tampering can be outside the check. Fix: HMAC with a key held outside the log (or external append-only anchoring), recompute every digest, page through the full chain.

docs.title: H-10 — Unsafe deserialization at checkpoint/model boundaries [R]
docs.text: checkpoint_manager.py:168-190 (pickle.load, pickle.loads), trainer_v2.py:456, fsdp.py:282, model.py:92, model_hub/converters/pytorch.py:20, model_hub/converters/huggingface.py:40,171 (torch.load(..., weights_only=False)). Loading an untrusted artifact executes arbitrary code via pickle reduction. Model-hub download flows make untrusted artifacts realistic inputs. Not a remote unauth RCE by itself (no endpoint confirmed auto-converting downloads), but a real code-execution primitive. Fix: default to safetensors/native format; make pickle opt-in (allow_unsafe=True) with prominent warnings; weights_only=True unless legacy formats require otherwise; signature-verify artifacts before loading.

docs.title: H-11 — Model Hub API key lifecycle broken [R]
docs.text: model_hub/api/main.py:252-261, :290-299; model_hub/api/models.py:344-378. Raw keys persisted (key_dict["raw_key"] = _raw). verify_api_key() checks only the hash: ignores is_active, expires_at, and scopes; no route enforces scopes. Revoked/expired keys keep working and a nominal read key can upload/delete. Fix: store only prefix + hash; reject inactive/expired keys; enforce scopes in dependencies; return raw key once at creation.

docs.title: H-12 — SNEPPX_update_verifier_check return convention contradicts its header [R]
docs.text: security/updates/signed_update.c:157-166 returns 1 for a valid signature and 0 for disabled/missing-key/invalid; include/neural_core/security/signed_update.h:95-97 documents 0 on success, -1 on error. In-tree callers use == 1, so an external client following the header (if (check(...) == 0) install(u);) installs unsigned/tampered updates. Fix: rename to ..._is_valid returning a boolean, or change to 0/-1 consistently and update docs/tests.

docs.title: H-13 — Scheduler LR changes never reach optimizer parameter groups [R+]
docs.text: bindings/python/SneppX_ALG/interface_bindings/schedulers.py:39-50. step() updates optimizer.lr and optional set_lr, but Optimizer.step() reads group.get("lr", self.lr). Reproduced: opt.lr = 0.01, opt.param_groups[0]["lr"] = 0.1. All training silently uses the initial LR. Fix: assign group["lr"] = lr for every param_groups entry; keep the scalar only for compatibility.

docs.title: H-14 — Distributed collectives are no-ops for world_size > 1 [A, reproduced by agent]
docs.text: bindings/python/SneppX_ALG/interface_bindings/distributed.py:73-84. all_reduce returns its input, all_gather returns world_size copies of the local tensor, reduce_scatter returns the input. With WORLD_SIZE=2, all_reduce([1,2]) → [1,2] instead of [2,4]. Training runs with unreduced gradients and reports success. Fix: route to the NCCL/MPI backend or implement a real CPU fallback; fail loudly if unsupported.

docs.title: H-15 — FSDP reduce_gradients() discards the live gradient [A, reproduced by agent]
docs.text: bindings/python/SneppX_ALG/interface_bindings/fsdp.py:153-167. Stores a reduced shard in sp.grad_shard then executes param.grad = None with no restore path. Observed param_grad None, grad_shard [0.5, 0.5]. The optimizer steps on a parameter with no gradient. Fix: keep or restore param.grad before the optimizer step.

docs.title: H-16 — NCCL backend uses a zeroed unique ID and reports success without communicating [A]
docs.text: net/distributed/nccl.c:120, :167-170, :204-227, :273-315, :337-367. ncclGetUniqueId is loaded but never called; rank 0 never broadcasts a real ID; loaded = 1 is set even when all dlsym results are NULL. CPU "fallbacks" copy local data or return 0 without sending. Allocation count * sizeof(float) is unchecked. Multi-rank jobs silently train on unreduced gradients. Fix: real unique-ID broadcast, validate symbols, return -1 for unsupported collectives, checked arithmetic.

docs.title: 3. Medium and low security / assurance findings
docs.text:
Location/line numbers for [A] items are as reported by the specialist pass; re-confirm before editing.

ID Sev Status Location Finding → minimal fix M-1 Medium [R] crypto_symmetric.py:97-103 Poly1305.mac is truncated SHA-256, not RFC 8439; verify is non-constant-time. → use real Poly1305/compare_digest. M-2 Medium [A] crypto_asm.py:129-144 Poly1305ASM clamps r with ...FFFF... instead of RFC 8439 ...C...C...7; forgeries possible. → correct mask + KAT. M-3 Medium [A] api_key_manager.py:82-134; security_middleware.py:52-65 60 s cache ignores expires_at; auth mode defaults to "none" → anonymous; static keys compared with in. → re-check expiry, fail closed, compare_digest. M-4 Medium [A] s5_safety.py:372-602 Several ctypes S5 calls ignore C return codes / out_len, returning buffers as valid defense output. → check every status, fail closed. M-5 Medium [R] container_security.py:721,754,793 update_id used as a path component without validation → traversal in staging/install. → allowlist chars / resolve-and-contain. M-6 Medium [A] audit_logger.py:390-464, :472-521, :571-595 Configurable endpoint gets Bearer token and follows redirects (SSRF + key exfil); retry buffer unbounded; table_name interpolated into SQL. → allowlist HTTPS endpoint, disable redirects, bound queue, validate identifier. M-7 Medium [A] differential_privacy.py:25-49, :236-344 DP noise from legacy global NumPy MT19937; DPSGD accepts epsilon but never spends/checks the budget → DP guarantee unenforced. → CSPRNG + enforce budget per step. M-8 Medium [A] crypto_hash.py:53-70; secure_updates.py:5,36-65,106-108 "BLAKE3" is silently SHA-256 in this install (blake3 not a dependency); keyed hash/derive ignore the key. Signed digest algorithm changes silently if blake3 is installed. → declare dependency or rename API. M-9 Medium [A] key_vault.py:129-139; audit_logger.py:257-285,763-769 wrap_key() is unauthenticated XOR; missing key silently XORs with fresh random (unrecoverable). audit_logger.log() swallows all backend failures; file rotation breaks chain continuity. → AEAD wrapping, surface write errors, persist chain head. M-10 Medium [A] s4_extensions.c:161,249,403,1131,1703; differential_privacy.c:45,60; s6_extensions.c:313,595,661; memory_hardening.c:225,341; side_channel_shield.c:90 Security-sensitive values (ClientHello random, "WireGuard key", gRPC token, DP noise, "HSM RNG") generated with rand(). → SNEPPX_random_bytes, fail closed. M-11 Medium [A] security/crypto/c/entropy_pool.c:142,166-179 OS entropy failure silently seeds rand() with time() and labels it OS; extraction cycles 8 SipHash bytes and substitutes TSC → predictable, no forward secrecy. → real DRBG, fail on OS error. M-12 Medium [A] security/memory/secure_allocator.c:111,156-161,360,409,446-484 Tracking-table full after 1024 allocations → add_record failure ignored, frees no longer scrub/free; g_record_count never decremented; bytes + overhead unchecked. → fail on add_record, reuse records, checked arithmetic. M-13 Medium [A] continuous_batching.py:64-86,106-179; inference_server.py:639-695 Global scheduler shared across requests; _next_id incremented outside lock; max_total_tokens unused; queues unbounded; endpoint discards results with pass so _completed is never drained. → isolate per request, bound queues, lock IDs, drain results. M-14 Medium [A] inference_server.py:68-99,551-636,727-823 async def endpoints call blocking generate(); BatchGenerateRequest.max_new_tokens unbounded; no prompt length cap; "too_long" filter result ignored. → bounds + worker pool + reject "too_long". M-15 Medium [A] serving_engine.py:648-756, :49-57 Stdlib server exposes deploy/traffic/generate with no auth; _body() trusts Content-Length; unguarded json.loads/int(). Loopback default limits exposure. → auth, body cap, validation. M-16 Medium [A] net_bindings.py:96-190 SocketComm.bind() hardcodes 0.0.0.0; framing length up to 0xFFFFFFFF accepted with no cap/timeout/auth; recv_tensor multiplies rows*cols before validation. → loopback default, size caps, timeouts, peer auth. M-17 Medium [A] model_hub/api/main.py:370-377 CORSMiddleware(allow_origins=["*"], allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"]). APIs use Authorization headers so not standalone ATO, but over-permissive. → explicit allowlist. M-18 Medium [R] docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:425,446,461,468,475,482,489,496,503,510 vs SECURITY.md:40-49 All ten layers marked Status: Complete; SECURITY.md says experimental/partial/incomplete/not verified/not audited. Materially overstates assurance. → sync statuses, add Alpha banner. M-19 Medium [A] .gitignore:91-92; .pre-commit-config.yaml; scripts/pre-commit.sh:27-34 No general secret scanner in pre-commit or CI; .env, *.pem, *.key are explicitly not ignored. Only PEM headers + AWS IDs + password= detected locally. → add ignore patterns + gitleaks hook + CI full-history scan. M-20 Medium [A] docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:440-442 vs docs/api/autodoc.md:10-12 PQC labelled FIPS 203/204/205 though repo says implementations are experimental and not interoperable; KAT docs confirm byte incompatibility. → relabel as round-3 with caveat. M-21 Low [R] Dockerfile (whole file); docker-compose.yml:42-53 No USER directive → runtime images run as root (sibling Dockerfile.cpu does it correctly). → add non-root user. M-22 Low [A] security.txt:1-9 PEM-style BEGIN SECURITY CONTACT markers are non-standard for RFC 9116; may break researcher parsers. → plain Field: value, publish at .well-known/security.txt. M-23 Low [A] Dockerfile:7,43,72,98,126; docker-compose.yml:53 Floating base-image tags, pip install uvicorn at container start with no version/hash, no Dependabot config. → digest pins, pinned deps at build, Dependabot. M-24 Medium [R] security/updates/container_security.c:94-117 strncmp(p, "\"config\":", 9) on a length-bounded, possibly non-NUL-terminated buffer → OOB read; manifest digest is 64 random hex chars from rand() (:114). → length checks with memcmp, content-derived digest. M-25 Low [A] net/http/vizmon.c:713-724, :1273-1283 json_escape does not escape <, >, &, U+2028/9; snapshot injected into inline <script> → possible </script> breakout if tags are attacker-influenced. → escape for script context + CSP. M-26 Low [A] bindings/python/bindings/autograd_bindings.cpp:65-66; tensor_bindings.cpp:139-158 PyVariable::get_data/get_grad return non-owning PyTensor views; NumPy view keeps wrapper alive but not the tape/variable owning the memory → potential use-after-free. Needs review (no compiler here). → owning copies or keep_alive tied to the actual owner.

docs.title: 4. Correctness bugs (wrong results, silent training failures)
docs.text:
All were reproduced with small CPU-only scripts by the specialist pass; items marked [R]/[R+] were independently confirmed here.

ID Sev Status Location Observed vs expected → fix B-1 High [R+] grad_checkpoint.py:75,83-85 checkpoint_sequential([f0,f1,f2,f3], segments=2) → 40.0, expected 28.0. functions[i::segments] interleaves layers. → contiguous slices. B-2 High [R+] data_loader.py:249-267, :160-167 DataLoader(range(6), batch_size=3, num_workers=2) → six batches of size 1. Multi-worker path collates single samples. → batch indices before dispatch. B-3 High [R] data_loader.py:64-85 dtype="int16" sets itemsize=2 but np.frombuffer(buf, dtype=np.int32) reinterprets pairs → shape (2,) int32 instead of (4,) int16. → single dtype map. B-4 Medium [R+] nn.py:239-265 state_dict() omits non-persistent buffers but load_state_dict(strict=True) includes them → RuntimeError Missing key(s): ['tmp']. → named_buffers(persistent=True) in loader. B-5 High [R+] nn_functional.py:343-355 F.embedding(..., padding_idx=0) neither zeros the padding row nor attaches a graph (grad is None). → extend EmbeddingFn with paddingidx/maxnorm. B-6 High [A] optim.py:323-337 Adamax omits bias correction: first step moves by 0.1·lr·g instead of lr·g. → m_hat = m/(1-beta1**step). B-7 High [A] optim.py:487-514 ASGD(average_pars=True) zeroes parameters on the first step (5.0 → 0.0, expected ≈4.9). → seed ax from initial parameters. B-8 High [A] optim_extra.py:84-109 LAMB._t() called twice per parameter per step → identical params with identical grads get different updates. → compute t once per step. B-9 High [A] optim_extra.py:328-349 Sophia.estimate_hessian uses scalar (loss+ - loss-)/(2eps), which is ∇f·z, not Hz, and ignores the grads argument → wrong Hessian (observed [-5,5], expected [1,4]). → differentiate gradients. B-10 Medium [A] checkpoint_manager.py:106-113,133-139; amp.py:70-72 Manager assumes PyTorch-style writable gradScaler.scale/growth_factor; shipped GradScaler has read-only scale and _growth_factor → save/restore raises AttributeError. → use backing fields or add setters. B-11 Medium [A] optim.py:83-104 state_dict() omits param-groups; after restore, group LRs stay at corrupted values ([999,999]). → serialize/restore group hyperparameters. B-12 Medium [A] nn_functional.py:993-1012 F.pad_sequence() builds a raw NumPy array → grad is None. → differentiable padding/Function. B-13 Medium [A] advanced_ops.py:320-370 avg_pool2d(count_include_pad=False) infers padding from window != 0, so genuine zero activations are excluded from the denominator (3.0 instead of 1.5). → padding mask by position. B-14 Medium [A] advanced_ops.py:629-640 cross_entropy() returns per-sample losses while documenting mean reduction ([0.313, 0.0486] instead of [0.1809]). → add reduction arg or return mean. B-15 Medium [A] init.py:108-111 xavier_uniform_ bound sqrt(3/(fan_in+fan_out)) instead of sqrt(6/(...)) → ~0.707× intended variance. → change 3.0 to 6.0. B-16 Medium [A] autograd_ops.py:4747-4784 TripletMarginLoss accepts p but always computes L2; p=1 gives 2.586 instead of 2.0. → save/use p in forward and backward. B-17 Medium [A] functional.py:17-22 _as_tensor([1,2]) raises NameError: _resolve_dtype is not defined. → import/define dtype resolver. B-18 Low [A] rng.py:19 set_global_seed() writes SNEAPX_SEED (typo) instead of SNEPPX_SEED. → fix key (keep old temporarily). B-19 High [A] quantization.py:54-64,435-453 quantize_int8_asym clips vmax for all-positive ranges (4.0 → 3.0); QuantizedLinear.forward ignores self.mode/zero-point (asym [[3,6]] vs [[3,7]]) and feeds packed INT4 weights to INT8 dequantization (output [95.4] vs [[3,7]]). → joint scale/zero-point selection, store zero-point/shape, dispatch on mode.

docs.title: 5. Deliberate stubs / no-ops — do not rely on these as security controls
docs.text:
These are not "exploitable bugs" in themselves, but several are exported under security-sounding names and will produce false assurance.

  • crypto_kem.py — Kyber KEM and X25519 fallbacks (see C-4).
  • crypto_symmetric.py — AEAD fallbacks and Poly1305 (see C-5, M-1).
  • crypto_asm.py — Ed25519ASM.sign produces R_y || s without the RFC 8032 sign bit and has no verifier; AESNI ignores rounds/round-key semantics.
  • secure_memory.py:85-106 — w_xor_x() always True, guard_page() returns a random int, seccomp_filter() always False (docstring says no-ops).
  • ai_safety_ext.py:41-59 — check_factuality() always 0.8, detect_semantic_injection() and detect_membership_inference() always 0.0.
  • s5_safety.py:416-419 — S5PromptFilter.sanitize() returns text unchanged (detection-only).
  • formal_verify.py:85-144 — ModelChecker reduces any formula containing "always"/[]/g to "is error state reachable"; reports success for properties it never evaluated.
  • security/network/transport_security.c:225-241 — Noise handshake is 48 random bytes XORed with a fixed-key-derived value; no DH, transcript, or authentication.
  • security/network/s4_extensions.c:841-851 — SNEPPX_mtls_verify_chain compares at most 8 bytes at fixed 32-byte strides (also an unchecked OOB read for long chains).
  • security/hardware/side_channel_shield.c:76-81 — SNEPPX_hsm_verify_measurement always returns 0.
  • bindings/python/SneppX_ALG/interface_bindings/nccl.py:78-103,138-153 and net_bindings.py:193-311 — collectives/RDMA/NCCL send/recv are CPU fallbacks or no-ops.
  • acvp_kat.py:86-95 — load_kat(name) joins unchecked name → arbitrary JSON read in the test harness (low severity).

docs.title: 6. Verified OK / negative results
docs.text:
Worth recording so later fix work does not "fix" non-problems:

  • No live hardcoded credentials, API keys, tokens, AWS keys, or PEM private keys in tracked files. Matches found are documented placeholders or detector fixtures.
  • CI workflows are unusually well hardened: contents: read on test/lint/package, third-party actions pinned to 40-char SHAs, persist-credentials: false, no pull_request_target, no self-hosted, no id-token: write, no shell injection via ${{ }}.
  • .dockerignore excludes key/credential patterns; no privileged, host network, or docker.sock mounts.
  • security/crypto/c/ed25519.c is a real Edwards-curve implementation with point validation, canonical-S checks, and constant-time comparison; SHA-512 and random.c look sound.
  • crypto_sign.py fails closed when its native backend is missing — the pattern the other crypto modules should copy.
  • api_key_store.py hashes keys at rest; api_key_manager.py uses compare_digest and invalidates its cache on revoke/update; model_hub/api/client.py and serving_client.py refuse to send keys over non-local plain HTTP.
  • serve_cli.py blocks --auth-mode none on non-loopback binds.
  • yaml.safe_load used for config; SQLite value queries are parameterized.
  • SQL injection: none found; command injection via shell=True: none found in the audited Python security paths.
  • TripletMarginLoss p=2 gradients match finite differences; ReduceLROnPlateau itself reduces its internal base LRs correctly (the bug is only propagation, H-13).
  • Working tree unchanged after the audit; no commits or pushes made.

docs.title: 7. Recommended fix order (micro-commit friendly)
docs.text:
Each line is a candidate self-contained commit with its own per-file test. Re-run the affected test file before committing/pushing.

Wave 1 — fail-open and fake primitives (code execution / authentication):

  1. C-1 container verify: require Ed25519, reject empty signature (+ C test).
  2. C-2 Python update install: enforce verified, reject missing signature (+ test).
  3. C-3 hub admin: remove default password, loopback bind, no raw key logging (+ test).
  4. C-6 inference server: wire lifespan, fail closed on _security is None (+ test).
  5. C-4/C-5/C-8: make fake KEM/AEAD/Argon2 raise instead of fabricating (+ tests).
  6. C-7 transport XOR: remove or fail closed (+ test).
  7. H-10: weights_only=True default / pickle opt-in (+ test).

Wave 2 — memory safety in C: 8. H-1 SBOM export capacity check (+ C regression with tiny buffer). 9. H-2 SBOM hash length/NULL checks (+ regression). 10. M-24 manifest length checks and real digest. 11. M-12 secure allocator checked arithmetic and record reuse. 12. H-4/H-5 transport rekey symmetry and AAD NULL paired decrypt.

Wave 3 — silent training corruption: 13. H-13 scheduler → param_groups (+ regression). 14. B-1 checkpoint chunking, B-2 multi-worker batching, B-3 int16 dtype. 15. H-14/H-15/H-16 distributed/FSDP/NCCL honesty. 16. B-6–B-19 optimizer/init/functional/loss correctness, one commit each.

Wave 4 — assurance and hygiene: 17. M-18/M-20 docs statuses and PQC labels. 18. M-19 secret scanner + ignore patterns. 19. M-21 non-root Docker user; M-22/M-23 security.txt and pins.

docs.title: 8. Limitations / verification notes
docs.text:
• No C compiler is available locally (gcc/cl/clang all empty), so C findings were verified by source inspection only. They are straightforward control-flow/arithmetic defects, but cannot be compiled or executed here. The pybind lifetime item (M-26) is explicitly Needs review.
  • Full pytest suite hangs in this environment; only per-file / direct one-liner verification was used. Suggested regression tests must be run per file with PYTHONPATH=bindings/python, PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.
  • No LLM/CUDA/inference-server tests were run (machine constraints in repo AGENTS.md).
  • A full git-history secret scan was not completed (too slow on this history). Working tree is clean; run gitleaks detect / trufflehog git file://. once as a one-off compensating control.
  • [A] findings carry specialist-pass line numbers; confirm against the current HEAD before editing because the repo recently went through a repo-wide formatting pass.

Bottom line: The repo's most dangerous problem is not missing features — it is security primitives that silently pretend to work and training paths that silently compute the wrong thing. Both classes are worse than an explicit error because callers have no signal. Fix Wave 1 before adding any new capability.

docs.title: 9. Resolution addendum (2026-11-23)
docs.text:
Status: RESOLVED — no Critical findings remain open at the current HEAD.

  1. All seven Critical findings (C-1 through C-7) verified fixed at the current HEAD during this follow-up program; the Critical section is closed and no new Critical findings were introduced by the CTM hardening wave.
  2. CTM tooling wave completed:
  3. Replaced all shebang-only stub tools in ctm_tools/py/ with working implementations, each covered by per-file regression tests and CLI smoke tests: ctm_count_functions, ctm_count_headers, ctm_diff_loc, ctm_list_large_files, ctm_recent_files.
  4. Added nine new tools: ctm_todo_scan, ctm_doc_links, ctm_duplicate_files, ctm_churn, ctm_license_inventory, ctm_schema_check, ctm_encoding_report, ctm_ignore_audit, ctm_trend.
  5. Added shared scanner helpers: ctm.text_files, ctm.iter_files, ctm.is_link (Windows junction-aware).
  6. Registered sneppx-ctm* console scripts via [project.scripts] and shipped the tools through the ctm_tools.py package (ctm_tools/py/__init__.py aliases).
  7. Hardened the HTML dashboard with a per-language bar chart and a skipped-file breakdown; scan reports now include skipped_by_reason.
  8. Fixed the Windows junction leak (reparse points were followed because Path.is_symlink() is false for junctions); added junction test coverage.
  9. Repaired docs: C-tool claims corrected, corrupted code fences restored, new tool surface documented in README.md, ctm_tools/README.md, and docs/tools/ctm-tools.md.
  10. Legacy script unification (in progress): simple legacy counters that duplicated scanner logic have been moved onto the shared helpers (ctm_count_total_loc, ctm_summary_report, ctm_count_total_files are now unified; the remaining focused scripts are being migrated or explicitly deprecated in favor of the unified scanner).
  11. Open non-blocking work: finishing legacy script migration, docs/gh-pages drift cleanup, and the true forward-mode JVP engine (reverse-of-reverse remains acceptable).

docs.title: 10. Section 5 false-assurance closure (2026-11-24)
docs.text:
Every stub listed in section 5 now either fails closed or documents its non-security status explicitly:

  • crypto_kem.py / crypto_symmetric.py: fake KEM, AEAD and Poly1305 paths raise RuntimeError instead of fabricating successful primitives.
  • crypto_asm.py: Ed25519ASM.sign now emits real RFC 8032 signatures and has a matching verifier; AESNI.encrypt_block validates round count and key length instead of silently ignoring them.
  • secure_memory.py: w_xor_x() returns False; the other hardening helpers are documented as no-ops and no longer imply protection.
  • ai_safety_ext.py: constant RLHF scores replaced with advisory heuristics that state they are not a safety control.
  • s5_safety.py: S5PromptFilter.sanitize() documents that it is detection-only and returns text unchanged.
  • formal_verify.py: unsupported LTL fragments fail closed; only the implemented safety/liveness fragments can report a pass.
  • security/network/transport_security.c: the fake Noise handshake fails closed; real Noise lives in noise_protocol_extended.{h,c}.
  • security/network/s4_extensions.c: SNEPPX_mtls_verify_chain fails closed instead of comparing 8 bytes at fixed strides (also removing the OOB read).
  • security/hardware/side_channel_shield.c: SNEPPX_hsm_verify_measurement fails closed.
  • nccl.py / net_bindings.py: collectives and point-to-point transfers are documented as single-process fallbacks; multi-rank send/recv fail closed.
  • acvp_kat.py: load_kat(name) accepts only a bare vendored *.json name, so it can no longer read arbitrary JSON files in the test harness.

Legacy CTM script unification also resumed: ctm_largest_files now delegates to ctm_find_large_files, and ctm_count_empty_files uses the shared ctm.iter_files filters, each with per-file regression coverage.

docs.title: CTM Tools
docs.text:
CTM (Codebase Telemetry & Metrics) provides a standard-library repository scanner plus standalone focused utilities for codebase telemetry.

The supported implementation is the dependency-free Python scanner:

sneppx-ctm /path/to/repo
sneppx-ctm /path/to/repo --format json --output ctm-report.json
sneppx-ctm /path/to/repo --format csv
sneppx-ctm /path/to/repo --format html --output ctm-report.html

docs.title: Current tool surface
docs.text:
Entry point Purpose sneppx-ctm Unified repository scanner (text/json/csv/html reports, schema v1) sneppx-ctm-functions Heuristic function-definition counts by language sneppx-ctm-headers C/C++ header and source file counts sneppx-ctm-diff Per-language LOC/bytes delta between two trees sneppx-ctm-large Largest included files with human-readable sizes sneppx-ctm-recent Most recently modified included files sneppx-ctm-todo TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX marker scan sneppx-ctm-links Relative Markdown link checker sneppx-ctm-duplicates Byte-identical file duplicate detection sneppx-ctm-churn Git-history change frequency per file sneppx-ctm-license SPDX/heuristic license header + manifest inventory sneppx-ctm-schema Validate CTM JSON reports against schema v1 sneppx-ctm-encoding BOM / invalid-UTF-8 / newline-style report sneppx-ctm-ignore Explain why files are excluded by the default filters sneppx-ctm-trend Record and chart successive CTM JSON reports

All tools accept a root directory, --format text|json|csv|html, --output, and, where relevant, --include-other-text. The standalone Python sources live in ctm_tools/py/ and the shipped behavior is shared through the ctm_tools.py import package plus sneppx-ctm* console scripts registered in pyproject.toml.

The C prototypes under ctm_tools/c/ are unbuilt legacy scaffolding and are not part of the supported tool surface.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
Interactive, runnable tutorials for SNEPPX-Algo. Each tutorial has a companion Jupyter notebook under docs/tutorials/notebooks/ that you can download and run:

$env:PYTHONPATH = "bindings/python"

The notebooks use the pure-Python / NumPy fallback where possible so they run without a compiled C backend. docs.title: Tutorial — Image Classification with SNEPPX
docs.text: Notebook: classification.ipynb (download)

docs.title: What you'll build
docs.text: A small MLP classifier trained on synthetic 8×8 image data, using the SNEPPX nn module and AdamW optimizer. You'll see how Tensor operator overloads, Linear, LayerNorm, and CrossEntropyLoss compose, and how to log loss with the built-in Profiler.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
$env:PYTHONPATH = "bindings/python"

import numpy as np
from SneppX_ALG import (
    Tensor, Module, Sequential, Linear, LayerNorm, GELU, Dropout,
    AdamW, CrossEntropyLoss, CosineAnnealingLR, Profiler, Timer,
)
HAS_C = __import__("SneppX_ALG")._HAS_C_BACKEND

docs.title: 1. Synthetic data
docs.text:
We use 8×8 "images" with 10 classes:

def make_data(n=640):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    X = rng.standard_normal((n, 64)).astype(np.float32)
    y = rng.integers(0, 10, size=(n,)).astype(np.int64)
    return Tensor.from_numpy(X), Tensor.from_numpy(y)

docs.title: 2. The model
docs.text:
class Classifier(Module):
    def __init__(self, in_dim=64, hidden=128, classes=10):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = Sequential(
            Linear(in_dim, hidden), GELU(),
            LayerNorm(hidden),
            Linear(hidden, hidden), GELU(),
            Dropout(0.1),
            Linear(hidden, classes),
        )
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x)

model = Classifier()

docs.title: 3. Train (needs C backend for backward)
docs.text:
X, y = make_data()
opt  = AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=2e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)
sched = CosineAnnealingLR(opt, min_lr=1e-5, max_lr=2e-3, total_steps=200)
prof = Profiler(enabled=True)

for step in range(200):
    idx = np.random.randint(0, X.shape[0], 64)
    xb, yb = X[idx], y[idx]
    with Timer(prof, "forward"):
        logits = model(xb)
        loss = CrossEntropyLoss()(logits, yb)
    if not HAS_C:
        print("C backend not available — skipping backward/step")
        break
    opt.zero_grad(); loss.backward(); opt.step(); sched.step()
    if step % 25 == 0:
        print(step, loss.item())
prof.print_summary()

docs.title: 4. Evaluate
docs.text:
def accuracy(model, X, y, batch=128):
    if not HAS_C:
        return 0.0
    correct = 0
    for i in range(0, len(X), batch):
        preds = model(X[i:i+batch]).data.argmax(-1)
        correct += (preds == y[i:i+batch].data).sum()
    return correct / len(X)

print("accuracy:", accuracy(model, X, y))

docs.title: Key takeaways
docs.text:
• Tensor overloads +, @, * — write math, not matmul() calls.
  • Linear uses PyTorch layout (out, in) weight, i.e. x @ W.T + b.
  • CrossEntropyLoss expects logits of shape (N, C) and targets (N,).
  • Without the C backend, backward()/step() are unavailable — build the extension first (cmake --build build --config Release).

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Swap Classifier for Transformer (see Generation).
  • Add DistributedWrapper for multi-GPU (see Distributed Training).

docs.title: Tutorial — Data Pipeline
docs.text: Notebook: data_pipeline.ipynb (download)

docs.title: What you'll build
docs.text: A complete data pipeline: train a SimpleTokenizer on text, encode/decode, batch with DataLoader + DistributedSampler, and serve batches to a model.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
$env:PYTHONPATH = "bindings/python"

import numpy as np, os
from SneppX_ALG import SimpleTokenizer, Tokenizer, Tensor
from SneppX_ALG.interface_bindings.data_loader import DataLoader, TensorDataset
HAS_C = __import__("SneppX_ALG")._HAS_C_BACKEND

docs.title: 1. SimpleTokenizer (no HF deps)
docs.text:
corpus = ["hello world sneppx", "hello neural engine", "sneppx is fast",
          "neural networks rock", "sneppx sneppx hello"]

tok = SimpleTokenizer(vocab_size=50)
tok.train(corpus, min_freq=1)
ids = tok.encode("hello sneppx")
print("ids:", ids)
print("text:", tok.decode(ids))

docs.title: 2. Production tokenizer (HF tokenizers JSON)
docs.text:
# If you have a tokenizer.json from HuggingFace:
if os.path.exists("tokenizer.json"):
    ptok = Tokenizer("tokenizer.json")
    print("vocab size:", ptok.vocab_size)
    print("bos/eos/pad:", ptok.bos_token_id, ptok.eos_token_id, ptok.pad_token_id)
    print(ptok.decode(ptok.encode("Hello, world!")))
else:
    print("no tokenizer.json present — using SimpleTokenizer")

docs.title: 3. Chat template formatting
docs.text:
ptok = Tokenizer(vocab_size=32000)     # falls back to SimpleTokenizer
messages = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are SNEPPX, a helpful assistant."},
    {"role": "user",   "content": "Summarize neural programming engines."},
]
prompt = ptok.apply_chat_template(messages)
ids = ptok.encode(prompt)
print(prompt)

docs.title: 4. TensorDataset + DataLoader
docs.text:
X = np.random.randint(0, 300, (200, 16)).astype(np.int64)   # token ids
Y = np.random.randint(0, 300, (200, 16)).astype(np.int64)   # labels
ds = TensorDataset(Tensor.from_numpy(X), Tensor.from_numpy(Y))
loader = DataLoader(ds, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)

for xb, yb in loader:
    print("batch:", xb.shape, yb.shape)    # (32, 16) (32, 16)

docs.title: 5. Streaming large corpora (mmap)
docs.text:
from SneppX_ALG.interface_bindings.data_loader import (
    MemoryMappedTextDataset, StreamingTokenDataset,
)

# Random-access over a huge file via mmap
mmap_ds = MemoryMappedTextDataset(path="big_corpus.txt", tokenizer=tok, seq_len=512)

# Streaming webdataset-style shard reader
stream = StreamingTokenDataset(path="data/shard_*.jsonl", tokenizer=tok, seq_len=1024)

docs.title: 6. Distributed sharding
docs.text:
from SneppX_ALG import DistributedSampler, get_world_size, get_rank

sampler = DistributedSampler(ds, num_replicas=get_world_size(), rank=get_rank(), shuffle=True)
loader  = DataLoader(ds, batch_size=32, sampler=sampler)
sampler.set_epoch(epoch)      # re-shuffle per epoch

docs.title: Key takeaways
docs.text:
• SimpleTokenizer (word-level) needs no dependencies; Tokenizer wraps HF tokenizers for BPE/WordPiece when available.
  • Special tokens: <pad>=0, <unk>=1, <s>=2, </s>=3.
  • DataLoader lives in interface_bindings.data_loader — not re-exported via from SneppX_ALG import *.
  • apply_chat_template emits <|system|> / <|user|> / <|assistant|> tags.
  • CPU-safe throughout (no C backend needed for the data pipeline).

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Tokenize + generate text — see Text Generation.
  • Build a language-model dataset for distributed training — see Distributed Training.

docs.title: Distributed Training: Support Status
docs.text:
This page records the current state of distributed training so examples do not overstate what the implementation can execute.

Multi-rank training is unsupported.

The Python distributed module currently provides environment metadata and a deterministic sampler utility. It does not yet initialize a real multi-rank process group, synchronize gradients, or gather sharded parameters. APIs that would otherwise make a multi-rank run appear successful now fail closed.

docs.title: Safe local check
docs.text:
from SneppX_ALG import DistributedSampler

dataset = list(range(12))
sampler = DistributedSampler(
    dataset, num_replicas=3, rank=1, shuffle=False
)
assert list(sampler) == [1, 4, 7, 10]

This checks local index partitioning only. It is not a distributed training test.

docs.title: Required work before a distributed release
docs.text:
1. Implement a process-group lifecycle with validated rank membership.
  2. Implement and test CPU collectives before adding accelerator transport.
  3. Implement NCCL communicator creation, unique-ID exchange, and error checks.
  4. Prove DDP gradient synchronization with deterministic multi-process tests.
  5. Complete FSDP/ZeRO parameter and optimizer-state sharding, including checkpoint and failure-recovery semantics.
  6. Test pipeline, tensor, and expert parallel execution across actual processes.

Do not use WORLD_SIZE greater than one, FSDP, ZeRO, or the launch helper for production training until these milestones are complete.

docs.title: Tutorial — RLHF Fine-Tuning with LoRA + DPO
docs.text: Notebook: fine_tuning_rlhf.ipynb (download)

docs.title: What you'll build
docs.text: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning recipe that (1) attaches LoRA adapters to a small model, (2) trains with DPO (Direct Preference Optimization) via SneppX_ALG.DPOTrainer, and (3) exercises the S5 AI safety filter on the generated output.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
$env:PYTHONPATH = "bindings/python"

import numpy as np
from SneppX_ALG import (
    Transformer, Tokenizer, AdamW, Tensor,
    DPOTrainer, LoRAConfig, LoRALinear,
    S5RLHFSafety, S5OutputVerifier,
)
HAS_C = __import__("SneppX_ALG")._HAS_C_BACKEND

docs.title: 1. Attach LoRA adapters
docs.text:
LoRA freezes the base weights and injects low-rank A·B updates into attention projections.

base = Transformer(vocab_size=300, dim=128, num_heads=4, num_layers=4, ffn_dim=256, max_seq_len=64)

lora_cfg = LoRAConfig(r=8, alpha=32, dropout=0.1)
# Wrap a Linear in a LoRA-augmented layer
base.lm_head = LoRALinear(base.lm_head, r=lora_cfg.r, alpha=lora_cfg.alpha)
print("trainable params:", sum(p.numel for n, p in base.named_parameters() if "lora_" in n))

docs.title: 2. DPOTrainer
docs.text:
DPO optimizes the policy to prefer chosen over rejected completions.

trainer = DPOTrainer(
    policy=base,
    ref_policy=None,            # uses policy as its own reference on first call
    beta=0.1,
    optimizer=AdamW(filter(lambda p: p.requires_grad, base.parameters()), lr=5e-4),
)

# Toy preference data: (prompt, chosen_tail, rejected_tail) token-id lists
prefs = [
    ([1, 2, 3], [10, 11, 12], [99, 98]),
    ([4, 5, 6], [20, 21],    [88, 87, 86]),
]
for prompt, chosen, rejected in prefs:
    if not HAS_C:
        print("C backend required for DPO backward — skipping")
        break
    loss = trainer.dpo_loss(
        prompt_input_ids=prompt,
        chosen_input_ids=chosen,
        rejected_input_ids=rejected,
    )
    trainer.optimizer.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    trainer.optimizer.step()
    print("dpo loss:", float(loss.data))

The DPO loss is loss = -log_σ(β·(logπ(y_w|x) − logπ(y_l|x) − (β/r)·logπ_ref/ratio)). DPOTrainer._forward_logps computes log-probs with proper softmax.

docs.title: 3. GRPO alternative
docs.text:
from SneppX_ALG import GRPOTrainer

grpo = GRPOTrainer(
    policy=base,
    optimizer=AdamW(base.parameters(), lr=3e-4),
    num_generations=4,
    beta=0.01,
)
# grpo_loss = ratio-based PPO surrogate; see trainer_v3

docs.title: 4. Safety-check the output
docs.text:
Run the generated continuation through the S5 safety layers:

prompt = "Explain how to..."
verifier = S5OutputVerifier()
safe = S5RLHFSafety(allowed_topics=["science", "technology"])
# After generation, verify + filter:
#   verifier.check(output_text)   -> bool
#   safe.is_safe(output_text)     -> bool

docs.title: Key takeaways
docs.text:
• LoRA keeps the full model frozen and trains only injected low-rank weights — cheap to checkpoint/export.
  • DPO needs backward() (C backend). GRPO is the PPO-style alternative.
  • Always run S5OutputVerifier / S5RLHFSafety before serving RLHF-tuned output (S5 layer).
  • Checkpoints are small (only adapter weights); merge via apply_lora.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Quantize the fine-tuned model — see Quantization + Serving.
  • Serve with sneppx-serve --rlhf-safety to apply S5 filters at the API.

docs.title: Tutorial — Text Generation
docs.text: Notebook: generation.ipynb (download)

docs.title: What you'll build
docs.text: A minimal causal-LM generation loop using the SNEPPX Transformer and the sampling/beam-search utilities in SneppX_ALG.interface_bindings.generation.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
$env:PYTHONPATH = "bindings/python"

import numpy as np
from SneppX_ALG import Transformer, Tokenizer, Tensor
from SneppX_ALG.interface_bindings.generation import (
    generate, GenerationConfig, TextStreamer, TokenStreamer,
)
HAS_C = __import__("SneppX_ALG")._HAS_C_BACKEND

docs.title: 1. A tiny model
docs.text:
We keep vocab/size small so the NumPy path is fast enough to preview behavior.

model = Transformer(
    vocab_size=200, dim=64, num_heads=4, num_layers=2,
    ffn_dim=128, max_seq_len=64, dropout=0.0,
)
model.eval()

docs.title: 2. Greedy search (do_sample=False)
docs.text:
cfg = GenerationConfig(max_new_tokens=24, do_sample=False)
ids = [1, 2, 3]                       # BOS, token, token
out = generate(model, ids, generation_config=cfg)
print(out["output_ids"])              # (1, 3 + 24)

docs.title: 3. Sampling with top-k + top-p
docs.text:
cfg = GenerationConfig(
    max_new_tokens=48,
    do_sample=True,
    temperature=0.8,
    top_k=40,
    top_p=0.9,
    repetition_penalty=1.15,
)
out = generate(model, ids, generation_config=cfg)
print("final length:", out["output_ids"].shape)

generate picks the strategy automatically:

Condition Strategy num_beams > 1 beam search do_sample and temperature > 1e-6 sampling (top-k/top-p) otherwise greedy

docs.title: 4. Beam search
docs.text:
cfg = GenerationConfig(
    max_new_tokens=32,
    num_beams=3,
    length_penalty=0.7,
    early_stopping=True,
)
out = generate(model, ids, generation_config=cfg)

docs.title: 5. Stream tokens live
docs.text:
tok = Tokenizer(vocab_size=200)
stream = TextStreamer(tokenizer=tok, skip_prompt=True)
out = generate(model, ids, generation_config=GenerationConfig(max_new_tokens=40), streamer=stream)
# tokens print as they are produced

For raw IDs instead of text, swap TextStreamer for TokenStreamer and read stream.get_tokens().

docs.title: 6. Batch generation (variable-length prompts)
docs.text:
from SneppX_ALG.interface_bindings.generation import batch_generate

prompts = [[1,2,3], [1,4,5,6,7], [1,8,9]]
cfg = GenerationConfig(max_new_tokens=16, temperature=0.7)
out = batch_generate(model, prompts, generation_config=cfg)
print(out["output_ids"].shape)       # (3, max_len + 16)

docs.title: Key takeaways
docs.text:
• generate expects a model whose forward(input_ids=..., past_key_values=..., use_cache=True) returns {"logits", "past_key_values"}; Transformer returns logits directly, so wrap it for true KV-cache decoding in production (see docs/API.md).
  • CPU-safe NumPy sampling loop works without the C backend — just slower.
  • repetition_penalty, top_k, top_p, and stop_strings are all configurable via GenerationConfig (or **kwargs override).

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Pair with a real Tokenizer (HF tokenizers JSON) — see Data Pipeline.
  • Serve the model with sneppx-serve — see Quantization + Serving.

docs.title: Tutorial — Model Conversion (HF → SNEPPX)
docs.text: Notebook: model_conversion.ipynb (download)

docs.title: What you'll build
docs.text: Convert a HuggingFace-style model directory (.safetensors + config.json) into a SNEPPX checkpoint (.sneppx) using convert_hf_to_sneppx, inspect the weight-name remapping, and load it back with CheckpointReader.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
$env:PYTHONPATH = "bindings/python"
# You need an HF model dir on disk (safetensors + config.json).
# Example: download via `huggingface-cli download` or use a local copy.

import os, json, glob
from SneppX_ALG import (
    from_pretrained, get_model_config, list_available_models,
    read_safetensors, convert_hf_to_sneppx, HF_WEIGHT_MAP,
)
from SneppX_ALG import CheckpointReader, validate_checkpoint
HAS_C = __import__("SneppX_ALG")._HAS_C_BACKEND

docs.title: 1. Pick a supported family
docs.text:
print(list_available_models())     # ['llama2:7B', 'llama2:13B', 'llama3:8B', 'mistral:7B', 'qwen2:7B', ...]

cfg = get_model_config("mistral", "7B")   # config + param estimate
print(cfg["hidden_size"], cfg["num_hidden_layers"], cfg["num_attention_heads"])

docs.title: 2. Inspect the weight name map
docs.text:
print("HF -> SneppX name remaps (non-layer):")
for hf_name, sx_name in HF_WEIGHT_MAP["mistral"].items():
    print(f"  {hf_name:40s} -> {sx_name}")

Layer weights follow the pattern:

model.layers.{i}.{submodule}.weight   ->   layers.{i}.{remapped}.weight
model.embed_tokens.weight            ->   embedding.weight
model.norm.weight                    ->   norm.weight
lm_head.weight                       ->   lm_head.weight

docs.title: 3. Read a safetensors file directly
docs.text:
meta, tensors = read_safetensors("models/mistral-7b/model.safetensors")
print("metadata:", meta)
print("tensors found:", len(tensors))
sample = next(iter(tensors))
print(sample, "bytes:", len(tensors[sample]))

docs.title: 4. Convert to a .sneppx checkpoint
docs.text:
n = convert_hf_to_sneppx(
    hf_dir="models/mistral-7b",
    family="mistral",
    output_path="/ckpts/mistral-7b.sneppx",
    verbose=True,
)
print(f"converted {n} weights")

convert_hf_to_sneppx writes via CheckpointWriter (binary format with header + tensor records + metadata), so the result is S7-signed-update ready. Missing weights are written as zero-byte placeholders and logged as WARNING.

docs.title: 5. Validate + read back
docs.text:
ok, errs = validate_checkpoint("/ckpts/mistral-7b.sneppx")
print("valid:", ok, "errors:", errs)

reader = CheckpointReader("/ckpts/mistral-7b.sneppx")
meta_out = reader.metadata()
print(meta_out["family"], meta_out["num_converted"])

# Read a specific tensor (returns numpy)
w = reader.read_tensor("layers.0.attn.q_proj.weight")
print(w.shape, w.dtype)

docs.title: 6. From a config dict → nn.Transformer
docs.text:
from SneppX_ALG import build_transformer_from_config

cfg = get_model_config("llama2", "7B")
model = build_transformer_from_config(cfg)    # nn.Module (NumPy path)
print("params:", sum(p.numel for p in model.parameters()))

docs.title: Key takeaways
docs.text:
• convert_hf_to_sneppx is the only supported path for real weights. from_pretrained returns a config dict, not weights.
  • HF_WEIGHT_MAP covers llama2, llama3, mistral, qwen2, deepseek_v2 (LLaMA-3 reuses LLaMA-2 mappings).
  • read_safetensors is a standalone TLV parser — no safetensors package required.
  • .sneppx checkpoints are S7-signed-update ready; verify with sneppx-analyze verify before serving.
  • CPU-safe (conversion is NumPy); loading weights into Transformer.forward for generation needs the C backend.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Quantize the converted checkpoint — see Quantization & Serving.
  • Inspect with the CheckpointReader in Checkpointing.

docs.title: Tutorial — MoE SER Expert Routing
docs.text: Notebook: moe_ser_routing.ipynb (download)

docs.title: What you'll build
docs.text: A sparse Mixture-of-Experts layer using SNEPPX's SER module: route each token to the top-2 of 8 experts, compute the load-balancing loss, and inspect the routing distribution to detect expert collapse.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
$env:PYTHONPATH = "bindings/python"

import numpy as np
from SneppX_ALG import SERModel, SERConfig, Tensor
HAS_C = __import__("SneppX_ALG")._HAS_C_BACKEND

docs.title: 1. Configure an 8-expert, top-2 MoE
docs.text:
cfg = SERConfig()
cfg.num_experts = 8
cfg.num_active  = 2        # top-k
cfg.input_dim   = 64
cfg.expert_dim  = 128
cfg.output_dim  = 64
cfg.top_k_method = 0       # softmax routing
cfg.load_balance_coef = 0.01
cfg.dropout_rate = 0.0

moe = SERModel(cfg, seed=42, num_layers=1)

docs.title: 2. Forward pass
docs.text:
x = Tensor.randn((4, 16, cfg.input_dim))   # (batch, seq, dim)
out = moe.forward(x)                         # (4, 16, 64)

docs.title: 3. Inspect routing weights
docs.text:
With the C backend, the router probabilities are exposed via the SNEPPXSERRouter; here we approximate the load-balancing signal with a pure-NumPy router replica:

if not HAS_C:
    # Pure-NumPy illustration of the top-k routing math
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    router_logits = rng.standard_normal((16, 8))      # (seq, num_experts)
    scores = np.softmax(router_logits, axis=-1)
    top2 = np.argsort(-scores, axis=-1)[:, :2]
    load = np.zeros(8)
    for t in range(16):
        load[top2[t]] += 1
    print("tokens-per-expert:", load.astype(int))

docs.title: 4. Load-balancing loss
docs.text:
# C backend: moe.load_balance_loss(routing_weights)
# Pure-Python approximation:
routes = np.zeros(8)
for t in range(16):
    routes[top2[t]] += 1
frac = routes / 16.0
p_avg = scores.mean(axis=0)
loss = float(np.sum(frac * p_avg) * cfg.load_balance_coef)
print("balance loss:", loss)      # lower + uniform is better

docs.title: 5. Stacked MoE layers
docs.text:
class MoETransformer(Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.inp = Linear(64, 64)
        self.moe = SERModel(SERConfig(), seed=1, num_layers=4)   # 4 stacked MoE layers
        self.out = Linear(64, 64)
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.out(self.moe.forward(self.inp(x)))

net = MoETransformer()

docs.title: Key takeaways
docs.text:
• num_active (top-k) must be ≤ num_experts; increasing k raises FLOPs linearly but improves quality.
  • load_balance_coef trades quality for uniform expert usage; 0.01 is the default in the C config.
  • Expert parallelism (EP) shards experts across GPUs — set ep_size = num_experts / tp_size in DistributedConfig.
  • Without the C backend (_HAS_C_BACKEND is False), SERModel.forward raises RuntimeError: C backend not available — the illustration above shows the equivalent NumPy math.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Combine with Distributed Training for EP across nodes (see algorithms/ser/core/gater.c all-to-all dispatch).
  • Add a learned MLP gater (use_mlp_gater=1 in SNEPPXSERConfig).

docs.title: Tutorial — Profiling & Benchmarks
docs.text: Notebook: profiling_benchmarks.ipynb (download)

docs.title: What you'll build
docs.text: Instrument a forward+backward pass with the Profiler/Timer, track peak memory with MemoryTracker, and run a regression benchmark with the sneppx-bench CLI.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
$env:PYTHONPATH = "bindings/python"

import numpy as np, time
from SneppX_ALG import (
    Transformer, Linear, GELU, Tensor, AdamW,
    Profiler, Timer, MemoryTracker, get_profiler, timeit,
)
HAS_C = __import__("SneppX_ALG")._HAS_C_BACKEND

docs.title: 1. Profile a region
docs.text:
model = Transformer(vocab_size=500, dim=256, num_heads=4, num_layers=4, ffn_dim=1024, max_seq_len=64)
x = Tensor.randn((8, 64))

prof = Profiler(enabled=True)
with Timer(prof, "forward"):
    out = model(x)
with Timer(prof, "loss"):
    loss = out.data.mean()      # pure-NumPy surrogate (no C backend needed)
prof.print_summary()

docs.title: 2. Global profiler + @timeit
docs.text:
g = get_profiler(); g.enabled = True
g.reset()

@timeit(g)
def step(x):
    return model(x)

for _ in range(5):
    step(x)
print(g.to_json())             # structured JSON for dashboards

docs.title: 3. Memory tracking
docs.text:
mt = MemoryTracker()
mt.start()
for _ in range(10):
    _ = model(x)
peak = mt.peak(); mt.checkpoint("after-10")
mt.stop()
print("peak bytes:", peak)

docs.title: 4. Benchmark with sneppx-bench (regression)
docs.text:
sneppx-bench run tests/python/test_tensor.py \
    --repeat 10 --save results/bench_$(git rev-parse --short HEAD).json
# Compare two runs:
sneppx-bench compare results/bench_a.json results/bench_b.json

Flags: --repeat N, --warmup N, --filter <regex>, --save PATH, --unit <ms|s|us>. The tool tracks regressions against a local history under ~/.sneppx/.

docs.title: 5. CPU timing (no C backend) — fallback
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from SneppX_ALG import Tensor

# When the C backend is absent we still get deterministic shapes; just time it.
t0 = time.perf_counter()
for _ in range(20):
    y = model(x)
dt = (time.perf_counter() - t0) / 20
print(f"fwd {dt*1000:.2f} ms")

docs.title: Key takeaways
docs.text:
• Profiler aggregates by named region; Timer is the context-manager form.
  • get_profiler() returns the global profiler reused by @timeit.
  • On CUDA, NVTX markers (SNEPPX_USE_NVTX) are emitted automatically — import into nsys / nvtx UIs.
  • sneppx-bench stores results tagged with the git SHA for regression diffs.
  • The C core also ships kernel/profiler.c (SNEPPX_Profiler) for C-side instrumentation; the Python Profiler is its mirror.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Profile the quantized model — see Quantization & Serving.
  • See Benchmarks for full performance tables.

docs.title: Tutorial — Quantization & Serving
docs.text: Notebook: quantization_serving.ipynb (download)

docs.title: What you'll build
docs.text: Quantize the weights of a small Transformer to INT4 (AWQ) and FP8, measure the error/SNR, estimate the on-disk size, and launch the sneppx-serve FastAPI server with an authenticated, quantized model.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
$env:PYTHONPATH = "bindings/python"
# Serving deps (optional):
python -m pip install "sneppx-alg[serve]"

import numpy as np
from SneppX_ALG import (
    Transformer, Tensor, AdamW,
    QuantMode, quantize_int8_sym, dequantize_int8_sym,
    quantize_int4_sym, dequantize_int4_sym,
    quantize_int8_channel, dequantize_int8_channel,
    awq_quantize, awq_scale_weights, quantize_error,
)
from SneppX_ALG.interface_bindings.quantized_serve import (
    QuantizedModelConfig, quantize_model_weights,
    dequantize_weights, estimate_model_size_mb,
)
HAS_C = __import__("SneppX_ALG")._HAS_C_BACKEND

docs.title: 1. A small model + its raw weights
docs.text:
model = Transformer(vocab_size=500, dim=128, num_heads=4, num_layers=2, ffn_dim=256, max_seq_len=64)
params = {name: p.data.copy() for name, p in model.named_parameters()}
print("FP32 size MB:", sum(v.nbytes for v in params.values()) / 1e6)

docs.title: 2. Per-tensor INT8 sanity check
docs.text:
w = Tensor.from_numpy(params["lm_head.weight"].astype(np.float32))
qw, scale = quantize_int8_sym(w)
wq = dequantize_int8_sym(qw, scale)
print("INT8 SNR (dB):", quantize_error(w, wq, metric="snr"))

docs.title: 3. Per-channel INT8 (lower error)
docs.text:
qw, scales = quantize_int8_channel(w, dim=-1)
wq = dequantize_int8_channel(qw, scales)
print("per-channel INT8 SNR:", quantize_error(w, wq, metric="snr"))

docs.title: 4. INT4 AWQ (activation-aware)
docs.text:
act_scales = Tensor.randn((w.shape[1],))           # per-input-channel act scale
qw, scales = awq_quantize(w, act_scales, group_size=64)
# (decode path: per-group dequant then matmul — see QuantizedLinear)

docs.title: 5. Quantize the whole model for serving
docs.text:
cfg = QuantizedModelConfig(
    quant_mode=QuantMode.INT4_SYM,
    skip_layers=["lm_head", "embedding.weight"],   # keep embeddings FP32
)
quantized = quantize_model_weights(params, cfg)
print("INT4 size MB:", estimate_model_size_mb(quantized))

docs.title: 6. Round-trip (quantize → dequantize → compare)
docs.text:
restored = dequantize_weights(quantized)
max_err = max(
    np.abs(restored[k].astype(np.float32) - params[k].astype(np.float32)).max()
    for k in ["layers.0.attn.q_proj.weight"]
)
print("max abs error:", max_err)

docs.title: 7. Serve with sneppx-serve
docs.text:
The quantized weights can be saved and loaded by the FastAPI server:

import json, numpy as np
# Save quantized weights as a .npz or safetensors; write a config.
np.savez("/tmp/q_model.npz", **{k: (v.weight.data if hasattr(v, "weight") else v)
                                for k, v in quantized.items()})
cfg_out = {"quant_mode": QuantMode.INT4_SYM, "skip_layers": ["lm_head"]}
json.dump(cfg_out, open("/tmp/q_config.json", "w"))
print("saved /tmp/q_model.npz + /tmp/q_config.json")

Then from the shell:

sneppx-serve --port 8000 --host 127.0.0.1 `
    --auth-mode api-key --api-keys "dev-key" `
    --model-config /tmp/q_config.json --checkpoint /tmp/q_model.npz `
    --disable-output-verify

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer dev-key" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_new_tokens":8,"do_sample":false}'

docs.title: Key takeaways
docs.text:
• QuantizedLinear.from_float is the fastest drop-in replacement for a single Linear layer.
  • Whole-model quantization via quantize_model_weights skips embeddings by default — never quantize the LM head if you want stable logits.
  • quantize_error(metric="snr") gives a single scalar for quality; aim for SNR > 20 dB for INT4.
  • sneppx-serve applies the S4/S5 firewall and prompt/output filters by default — pass --disable-* only in trusted environments.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Quantize a real HF model — see Model Conversion → convert_hf_to_sneppx.
  • Profile the quantized forward — see Profiling & Benchmarks.

docs.title: Tutorial — Security Scanning
docs.text: Notebook: security_scanning.ipynb (download)

docs.title: What you'll build
docs.text: Run the sneppx-analyze static vulnerability scanner on SNEPPX's own C source, inspect the report, and exercise the S0 post-quantum crypto bindings (Dilithium signing, Kyber KEM) from Python.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
# sneppx-analyze is a globally installed tool (sneppx-toolkit[all]):
python -m pip install "sneppx-toolkit[all]"

import json
from SneppX_ALG import Ed25519, Dilithium, KyberKEM, sha256, SecureAllocator
HAS_C = __import__("SneppX_ALG")._HAS_C_BACKEND

docs.title: 1. Scan source with sneppx-analyze
docs.text:
import subprocess

result = subprocess.run(
    ["sneppx-analyze", "scan", "algorithms/hss/core/",
     "--format", "c,h", "--json"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
report = json.loads(result.stdout) if result.stdout else {"findings": []}
print("findings:", len(report.get("findings", [])))
for f in report.get("findings", [])[:5]:
    print(f"  [{f['severity']}] {f['rule']} @ {f['file']}:{f['line']}")

Flags: --format c,h,cu,cpp, --fail-on <info|low|medium|high|critical>, --sarif report.sarif (GitHub-Code-scanning import), --output out.json.

The scanner is static only — it never executes the analyzed code, so it is safe on untrusted sources.

docs.title: 2. Experimental round-3 Dilithium signing (S0)
docs.text:
This implementation is not byte-compatible with finalized FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) and is not FIPS-validated.

if HAS_C:
    msg = b"SNEPPX-Algo release v1.2.0"
    dil = Dilithium(level=3)          # experimental round-3 Dilithium
    sig = dil.sign(msg)
    assert dil.verify(msg, sig), "signature invalid"
    print("Dilithium-3 OK, sig len:", len(sig))
else:
    print("C backend required for S0 crypto (build neural_security_c)")

docs.title: 3. Experimental round-3 Kyber key encapsulation (S0)
docs.text:
This implementation is not byte-compatible with finalized FIPS 203 (ML-KEM) and is not FIPS-validated.

if HAS_C:
    kem  = KyberKEM(k=768)            # experimental round-3 Kyber
    ct, sk = kem.encapsulate()
    ss = kem.decapsulate(ct)
    assert ss == sk, "KEM mismatch"
    print("Kyber-768 KEM OK")

docs.title: 4. Hash + secure memory attestation
docs.text:
digest = sha256(b"model-weights.bin")
print("sha256:", digest.hex())

if HAS_C:
    buf = SecureAllocator(8192).alloc()   # guard pages + mlock
    StackCanary().install()
leaks = MemoryLeakDetector().scan()
print("leaks:", leaks)

docs.title: 5. S7 signed-update attestation (CLI)
docs.text:
sneppx-analyze verify model.sneppx --expected-signer "release@snepx"

Verifies the Ed25519 manifest signature embedded by CheckpointWriter.

docs.title: Key takeaways
docs.text:
• sneppx-analyze covers buffer overflows, NULL derefs, integer overflows, uninitialized reads, and crypto-misuse patterns.
  • S0 crypto (Dilithium/Kyber) requires the compiled neural_security_c target.
  • S1 memory hardening (SecureAllocator, guard pages) is always on for the C path; the Python API raises if the backend is missing.
  • Never commit secrets — the scanner flags SNEPPX_secure_free violations (buffers not wiped before free).

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Read Security Layers for the full S0–S9 model.
  • See Security Cookbook for PQ key management recipes.
